meta.title: B1 skills mock 1
meta.sourceNote: Our own B1 English mock in the style of the listening and reading skills tests at Trinity ISE I level (CEFR B1): nine parts, 45 scored tasks (listening 1-20, reading 21-45) and one writing task. It is not the ISE task structure: the real ISE I papers are built differently, so use this set to practise B1 listening, reading and writing skills, not to rehearse the exam format. The texts and tasks are our own. The points shown at the end are our own guide, not an official pass mark.
meta.audioNote: There are no recordings for this set yet. Instead of guessing, read the transcript. The tasks stay the same. In a real listening test you hear each recording once or twice and cannot read it.

parts.label: Hören · Teil 1
parts.title: Understanding announcements and phone messages
parts.instruction: You will hear four announcements or messages. There is one question for each. Choose the best answer, a, b or c.

example.transcript: Hello, you have reached Northpark Leisure Centre. We are open from seven in the morning until nine at night, Monday to Friday, and from nine until six on Saturdays. We are closed on Sundays. Swimming costs four pounds fifty for adults and two pounds fifty for children.
example.question: When is the leisure centre closed?

items.transcript: Attention please. The fourteen twenty service to Leeds is delayed by about ten minutes because of a signal fault. It will now leave from platform 6, not platform 3. Passengers for Leeds should use the footbridge to reach platform 6. We apologise for the delay.
items.question: Which platform should passengers for Leeds go to?

items.transcript: Hello, this is Greenfield Surgery calling for Mrs Osei. Your appointment with Dr Walker tomorrow at nine o'clock has to be changed because Dr Walker is unwell. We can offer you Thursday at a quarter past two instead. Please phone us on 01632 960 118 and let us know if that suits you. Thank you.
items.question: Why is the surgery calling?
options: To give Mrs Osei her test results.
To tell her that the surgery has moved.

items.transcript: Good afternoon, shoppers. A reminder that this Friday the store will close at four o'clock instead of eight, because we are counting our stock. On Saturday we will be open as usual, from eight in the morning until eight at night. We apologise for any inconvenience and wish you a pleasant afternoon.
items.question: What will happen on Friday?
options: The shop will close earlier than usual.
The shop will open later than usual.
The shop will be closed all day.

items.transcript: Hi Ms Rahman, it's Sandra from the swimming club. Just a quick message about Saturday's trip to the lake. Please make sure Ben brings a towel and a warm jumper. There's no need to pack him any lunch, because we are providing sandwiches. We'll be back at about four o'clock.
items.question: What should Ben bring on Saturday?

parts.label: Hören · Teil 2
parts.title: Understanding short items from the radio
parts.instruction: You will hear five short items from the radio. There is one question for each. Choose the best answer, a, b or c.

items.transcript: Now the travel news. On the M62 between junctions 20 and 21, traffic is queuing for about six miles after a lorry shed part of its load. The left-hand lane is closed. If you can, use the A58 instead. Recovery crews expect the clean-up to take at least another two hours.
items.question: What has caused the problem on the M62?
options: A lorry that has lost part of its load.

items.transcript: And now the weather for tomorrow. It will be cloudy in the morning, with some rain in places. From lunchtime it will turn brighter from the west, and there should be sunny spells by mid-afternoon. Highs of fourteen to seventeen degrees. Overnight, temperatures will fall to around six.
items.question: What will the weather be like in the afternoon?

items.transcript: A tip for the weekend: the town's spring festival returns to Central Park on Saturday. From eleven in the morning until ten at night there will be live music on two stages, food from around the world and activities for children. Entry is free. There is hardly any parking nearby, so the organisers recommend coming by bus.
items.question: What does the presenter say about the festival?
options: You have to pay to get in.
It is best to go by bus.

items.transcript: Passengers are warned that bus drivers have announced a strike for Tuesday. Local buses and school buses are not expected to run at all that day. The tram service is not affected and will run to its normal timetable.
items.question: What will still run on Tuesday?

items.transcript: And a reminder from the central library: from the first of June, the opening hours change. The library will open earlier, at ten, but it will close at one o'clock on Saturdays. Borrowing books stays free, although there will be a charge for items that are returned late.
items.question: What changes from 1 June?

parts.label: Hören · Teil 3
parts.title: Understanding everyday conversations
parts.instruction: You will hear four conversations. There are two tasks for each. In the first, decide whether the statement is true (richtig) or false (falsch). In the second, choose the best answer.

dialog: Excuse me, Mr Aydin, is that your washing in the machine downstairs? It's been sitting there since last night.
Oh no, I'd completely forgotten about it. I'm so sorry. I'll go and get it out now.
Don't worry. I just wanted to do a wash and the machine was in use.
I see. By the way, from next week there will be a sign-up sheet on the wall down there, so everyone can book a time.
That's a great idea. Then we'll all know whose turn it is.

questions.question: Mr Aydin forgot about his washing.
What will help from next week?
options: A key for the laundry room.

dialog: Good morning, how can I help?
Morning. I moved to the area last week and I'd like to join the library.
Of course. Have you got some photo ID and proof of your address, like a bill?
I've got my passport, but I haven't got anything with my new address on it yet.
In that case I can only give you a temporary card today. Bring in a bill or a bank letter within two weeks and we'll upgrade it.
Fine. I'll pop in again on Friday.

questions.question: Mr Novak has brought all the documents he needs.

dialog: Marina, would you fancy working my shift on Saturday? I'd take your Monday shift in return.
Saturday's no good, I've already got plans. But I could do Sunday.
Sunday doesn't help, I need Saturday off.
Why don't you ask Kemal? He wanted more hours anyway.
Good idea. I'll message him now.

questions.question: Marina will work Yusuf's shift on Saturday.
What does Marina suggest?
options: Asking Kemal to cover for him.

dialog: Hello, it's Ms Petrova. I need a repeat prescription for my tablets.
I'm afraid the doctor would like to see you first before issuing it.
Do I need to make an appointment? I work until five.
We have a drop-in clinic on Tuesdays and Thursdays until six, so you can come without booking.
Perfect, I'll come on Thursday after work.

questions.question: Ms Petrova can get her prescription over the phone.
When can she come without an appointment?
options: On Tuesdays and Thursdays until 6 pm.

parts.label: Hören · Teil 4
parts.title: Understanding people's opinions
parts.instruction: You will hear three people talking about how they learn English best. Which statement goes with which speaker? There are more statements than speakers.

statements.a: Talking to other people helps me most.
statements.b: I prefer to study on my own with an app.
statements.c: Watching series teaches me more than a course does.
statements.d: I can't manage without a regular class and a teacher.
statements.e: I learn mostly at work, without really trying.
statements.f: For me, writing is the most important thing.

example.transcript: I sit on the sofa with my phone for twenty minutes every evening. An app tests me on new words, and I can see straight away what I already know. A class would be too slow for me. I'd rather work at my own speed, on my own.

items.transcript: I tried studying on my own with books and videos, but after two months I'd forgotten nearly everything. Now I go to a class three times a week. There's a teacher who corrects me, and she notices when I'm missing. Without that kind of structure, I'd never keep going.

People always tell me to take a course, but honestly I've learned more from watching series. I put the English subtitles on and pause whenever I hear a new phrase, so that I can look it up. After a year I understood most things without any subtitles at all.

You can learn grammar from any book, that's not the problem. The hard part is having the courage to open your mouth. So every week I go to a conversation café and chat to complete strangers. After two hours I'm tired, but I've learned more than in a whole week of studying at home.

parts.label: Lesen · Teil 1
parts.title: Finding information in a contents page
parts.instruction: You are looking for information in a guide for newcomers to a town. In which chapter would you find it?

toc.title: Getting settled
toc.desc: Opening a bank account, council tax, proving your address, using the post office.

toc.title: Homes and neighbours
toc.desc: Understanding your tenancy agreement, household bills, recycling and bins, quiet hours in your building.

toc.title: Work and training
toc.desc: Having your qualifications recognised, employment contracts, looking for a job, careers advice.

toc.title: Health
toc.desc: Registering with a doctor, pharmacies, help out of hours and at weekends, children's vaccinations.

toc.title: Children and free time
toc.desc: Applying for a nursery or school place, clubs and groups for families.

example.question: You have just moved and need to open a bank account.

items.question: Your daughter starts school in September and you don't know how to apply for a place.
You worked as an electrician in your home country and want to know whether your qualification counts here.
Your child has a high temperature on Sunday and you don't know where to go.
Your neighbour complains because you run the washing machine at eleven at night.
You don't understand your gas and electricity bill.

parts.label: Lesen · Teil 2
parts.title: Matching situations to adverts
parts.instruction: Read the situations and the adverts. Which advert fits which situation? For one situation there is no suitable advert: choose 'keine' (none).

a.title: Maths tutor
a.body: Student teacher offers maths tutoring for Years 7 to 11. 15 pounds an hour, at your home or online. Available in the school holidays too. Call 07700 900 411.

b.title: Bike for sale
b.body: Ladies' bike, 7 gears, hardly used, a few scratches on the frame. 60 pounds or nearest offer. Collection only, Westgate area. Please text.

c.title: Flat to let
c.body: Two-bedroom flat with balcony, fourth floor (no lift), available from 1 May. 820 pounds a month plus bills. Non-smokers only, no pets.

d.title: Evening English class
d.body: English for adults, levels A2 to B1, Monday to Thursday, 6 to 8.30 pm. Suitable for people who work. Reduced fees for people on a low income. Enrol at the college reception, Room 12.

e.title: Cleaner wanted
e.body: Family with two children needs help twice a week for three hours, in the mornings. Experience preferred, good English not essential. 13 pounds an hour.

f.title: Man and van
f.body: Two strong helpers with a van, available at short notice, weekends too. From 35 pounds an hour including the van. Fixed price on request.

g.title: Children's clothes sale
g.body: Big sale of children's clothes and toys at Southfield Community Hall, Saturday 9 am to 1 pm. Good-quality clothes for ages 0 to 14, toys, pushchairs. Tea, coffee and cake on sale.

h.title: Dog sitting
h.body: Friendly retired woman will look after your dog while you are at work or on holiday. Overnight stays possible. Small garden. Free trial day.

items.question: You are going back to work next month and need someone to look after your dog during the day.
Your son is in Year 8 and is getting poor marks in maths.
You are moving house at the weekend and need someone to help carry the furniture.
You want to improve your English alongside your job and can only study in the evenings.
You are looking for a dentist who is open on Saturdays.

parts.label: Lesen · Teil 3
parts.title: Understanding short everyday texts
parts.instruction: Read the three texts. There are two tasks for each text. For the true/false tasks, choose richtig (true) or falsch (false).

texts.title: Email to parents
paras: As you know, Year 6 will spend three days at an activity centre in June. The cost is 95 pounds per child. If this is difficult for your family, please speak to me: there is a fund that can help. No child should miss out for financial reasons.
Important: the consent form and payment must reach me by 30 April. We cannot accept late bookings, because the centre will give the places to another school.

questions.question: Families with little money can get help.
What happens after 30 April?
options: It is no longer possible to book a place.

texts.title: Forum: is cycling to work worth it?
paras: Jo: I've started cycling to work and I love it. It takes 25 minutes, the same as the bus, and I'm saving about 50 pounds a month. My only worry is theft. My last bike was stolen outside the station.
Dev: I did the same for a year but gave up in winter. When it's dark and wet at five o'clock, I'd rather take the bus. If you carry on, buy good lights and lock your bike with two locks.
Mia: Don't give up! I leave work a bit earlier in winter and wear waterproof trousers. My employer even has a covered bike shed and a shower, so ask yours.

questions.question: Jo says cycling is faster than the bus.

texts.title: From the local newspaper: new community garden opens
paras: A disused car park in Bridge Street has been turned into a community garden. Since March, around thirty neighbours have built raised beds, planted fruit trees and set up a small compost area. The garden is open to everyone from dawn to dusk, and visitors are welcome to pick herbs and salad leaves for free.
'We wanted a place where people from different streets could meet,' says organiser Kofi Mensah. The project cost about 2,000 pounds, most of it paid by a local housing association and a cake sale.
Volunteers meet every Sunday from 10 am. No experience is needed and tools are provided, so newcomers can simply turn up.

questions.question: Visitors have to pay to pick herbs.
What is said about the volunteers?
options: They should bring their own tools.
They can join without any preparation.

parts.label: Lesen · Teil 4
parts.title: Understanding rules and regulations
parts.instruction: Read the text. Are the statements true (richtig) or false (falsch)?
paras: 3. Opening hours and peak times. The centre is open from 6 am to 10 pm on weekdays. Standard members may use the gym only between 9 am and 4 pm. Use of the gym at peak times (4 pm to 8 pm) requires a Premium membership. Children under 16 may use the pool only with an adult.

4. Lockers and belongings. Lockers may be used during your visit only and must be emptied by closing time. Anything left overnight will be removed and kept at reception for 14 days. The centre cannot be responsible for lost valuables.

5. Cancelling your membership. You can cancel at any time by giving one month's notice in writing, by letter or email. No refunds are given for unused days. For medical reasons, a membership can be frozen for up to three months if you bring a doctor's letter.

items.question: A Standard member can use the gym at 6 pm.
Anything left in a locker overnight is kept at reception for two weeks.
You can cancel your membership by phone.

parts.label: Lesen · Teil 5
parts.title: Completing an email
parts.instruction: Read the email. Which word fits which gap? Choose a, b or c.
parts.letterIntro: Folake Adeyemi is writing to her landlady.

letterSegments.text: in my flat last weekend. Water is running out from under the sink, and the cupboard below is already wet. I have turned off the stopcock

nothing worse happens.

I have tried to phone you

I am writing to you today.

Could you please
a plumber as soon as possible? I am at home every day this week after 3 pm and can let him in. I would be very grateful

a quick reply.

Yours sincerely
Folake Adeyemi

schreiben.instruction: Choose one of the two tasks. Write at least 40 words (80 to 100 words is a good length) and cover all four points. Start with a greeting and finish with a sign-off.

taskA.label: Task A
taskA.prompt: Your neighbour, Mrs Ford, is going to stay with her daughter for two weeks. She has asked whether you could feed her cat while she is away. Write a message back to her.
points: Say where you will keep the key
Ask what else you need to know
taskA.modelAnswer:
Hi Mrs Ford,

Of course I can feed Tilly while you're away. I'd be happy to. I can come every morning at about 7.30, before I leave for work, and again around 6 pm if she needs a second meal. Could I keep your spare key on the hook in my kitchen, so that it stays safe? Please let me know how much food she gets, whether she needs any medicine, and the vet's phone number in case of an emergency.

Have a lovely visit!
Amira
checklist: I gave times when I can come.
I said where the key will be.
I asked at least one question about the cat.
I used a greeting and a sign-off.
I checked my spelling and verb tenses.

taskB.label: Task B
taskB.prompt: You bought a washing machine three weeks ago. It does not work properly and you have already phoned the shop, but nothing has happened. Write an email to the shop.
points: What you want the shop to do
taskB.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about the washing machine I bought from your shop on 3 October (order number 4471). Since I installed it, the machine has not been spinning properly, and my clothes come out dripping wet. I phoned your customer service line last week, but nobody has contacted me since.

I would like you to send an engineer to repair the machine or, if that is not possible, to replace it. I would be grateful for a reply by Friday 13 November. I am at home in the afternoons on 07700 900 322.

Yours faithfully
Tomasz Wrona
checklist: I explained why I am writing in the first sentence.
I said what I want the shop to do.
I gave a date for the reply.
I used a polite, formal tone.
I checked my spelling and verb tenses.

schreiben.selfRateNote: A teacher would mark writing for content, organisation, language and how well it fits the reader. Here you can only judge your own text, and it is not saved or sent. Compare it with the checklist for the task you chose.
